notes: 250X300 / 10"X12" (note written at top-left of the sketch; no element identified against it)
5" / 125mm wall-thickness callout, written twice (top exterior wall and the BED ROOM 3 / BED ROOM 2 wall)
Room labelled 'Common Bath' on the first line with 'Lat' written and underlined beneath it; modelled as one room named 'Common Bath'.
'GATE' with '5'' written across the opening in the south exterior wall; 'Entry' with an up arrow written below it, outside the building.
assumptions: No north arrow or compass is drawn anywhere on the sketch. north_deg 90 is the schema default and is NOT read from the drawing.
The sketch is not titled as a particular floor. plan_name is given as 'FLOOR PLAN'; it is not written as 'GROUND FLOOR PLAN' on the sheet.
The only wall-thickness figure written anywhere is 5" / 125mm (twice). That value has been applied to every wall, internal and external, because no other thickness is called out.

The written dimension chains do not close exactly, as is normal on a hand sketch. Right-hand chain: 12'-0" + 12'-11" + 6'-7" + 4'-0" + 12'-0" = 47'-6" clear which with 5" walls gives 49'-7", against the written overall 50'-0" (5" short). Top chain: 11'-0" + 6'-4" + 11'-0" = 28'-4" clear, which with 5" walls gives 29'-7" against the written 30'-0" (5" short). The kitchen chain 11'-5" + 6'-4" + 11'-0" closes exactly on 30'-0", so the x grid has been set from that chain. Room boxes therefore run to the wall centre-lines and the size_label carries the figure exactly as written.

Left-hand chain conflict: 12'-0" (BED ROOM 4) + 8'-0" (KITCHEN) + 17'-4" (DWG/DINING HALL) + 12'-0" (DWG Living ROOM) plus walls comes to 51'-0", one foot more than the written 50'-0". The 12'-0" living-room depth was taken as governing because it is drawn level with the 12'-0" Guest Bed room on the same line and that chain closes; the dining hall therefore models at 16'-4" clear although '17'-4"' is what is written. The written figure is kept in its size_label.

KITCHEN has NO east wall. The sketch gives it 11'-5" clear over the same span for which BED ROOM 4 above it is given 11'-0" — a difference of exactly one 5" wall — and the kitchen's south wall is drawn ending in a free column with no wall running north from it. It is modelled open into the PASSAGE.

No wall is drawn across the north side of the staircase, so the stair mouth is left fully open to the DWG/DINING HALL (no wall and no opening listed there). A column is drawn on the west exterior wall at that line but no wall runs from it.

Staircase read as a U (half-turn / dog-leg): two parallel flights running in y, separated by a narrow well, with ONE landing — the square drawn and labelled 'Landing', 7'-0" x 3'-6" — at the south end. There is no short middle flight and no second landing, so it is not U3.

Stair direction traced from the arrows at the north end of the EAST flight: the UP arrowhead points north and the DN arrowhead points south, so the ascent finishes on the east flight. You therefore step on at the north end of the WEST flight, walk south to the landing, turn, and return north — hence up_from 'top', turn_side 'bottom'.

Tread counts (steps_f1 / steps_f2 = 10 each) were COUNTED off the drawn tread lines, not read. No riser or tread count is written. There is a short rotated mark on the west side of the flight that may read '10' or '16'; it could not be resolved and has not been used.
No window or ventilator carries any mark on the sketch. Every window is shown only as a yellow band across the wall. All are tagged 'W' for the software to number in reading order.
All window positions and widths were MEASURED against the written 30'-0" and 50'-0" overalls (scale approx. 33.6 px/ft in x, 34.4 px/ft in y). None of them is dimensioned on the sketch.

A yellow band is drawn on the internal wall between the PASSAGE and BED ROOM 2 (P-EAST-MID). It is reported as a window because every other yellow band on the sheet is a window, but an internal opening in that position is unusual and it is not labelled.

The kitchen door dimension reads as 3'-1" but the leading digit is ambiguous (it may be a 9). 3'-1" has been used. The drawn arc is smaller than that figure and does not fit between the drawn near jamb and the wall end, so pos has been set to seat the written width against the east end of the kitchen's south wall.

Every door symbol on this sketch is drawn noticeably smaller than the width written beside it. For each door, pos was derived from the CENTRE of the drawn arc minus half the written width, so the door sits where it is drawn at the width that is written.

The 4'-0" opening between DWG/DINING HALL and DWG Living ROOM is drawn with ONE leaf and ONE swing arc, so it is reported as single_door even though 4'-0" (1219 mm) is fractionally over the 1200 mm double-door threshold.

There is a small unlabelled space approx. 4'-0" x 4'-0" bounded by the DWG/DINING HALL to its west, the Common Bath to its north and the Toilet to its east. It is the lobby that the Common Bath door opens off. No name is written for it, so no room has been listed there; its bounding walls are listed.

The Toilet's west wall (P-TOI-W) is drawn as a short hatched strip with small rotated writing on it that could not be read. It has been placed at x 22.583 so the Toilet is exactly the written 7'-0" clear from the east exterior wall; the strip is drawn about 6 inches west of that.

The rectangle drawn outside the south wall under 'GATE', with an up arrow labelled 'Entry', is reported as entry steps. It shows about two treads and NO level marks are written on it, so 'levels' is left empty and 'count' 2 is counted from the drawn lines.
'Landing' is listed as a room because the sketch labels and dimensions it; it lies inside the staircase footprint and is the stair's landing, not a separate enclosure.
The 250X300 / 10"X12" note at the top-left is not attached by a leader to any element on the plan. It has been recorded verbatim in notes and not applied to any wall, beam or column.
No level marks, no plinth level, no door/window schedule, no plot boundary beyond the building line, and no setbacks are drawn anywhere on the sketch.
